narrative:

Surprisingly, the strongest influence came from your clean record of zero past failures. While this is identical to the average among students who passed, in your specific combination of circumstances the model interpreted it as insufficient to offset other risks. Your clear ambition to continue into higher education worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward passing. Similarly, reporting good family relationships also nudged the outcome positively, though not enough to change the final decision.

Because your past failures carried the heaviest weight and pulled toward failure, the model ultimately decided you need extra support. To improve, focus on turning your strong motivation for higher education into consistent daily study habits. Your current study time of less than two hours per week is well below what most successful students maintain. Reducing your nine absences, which already exceed the typical three to four days missed by passing students, would also help demonstrate reliability. Taking the remedial courses seriously gives you a clear opportunity to build better routines before the final exams.
